strings.name: Kelly Ortberg
strings.role: President and Chief Executive Officer of Boeing
strings.summary: Kelly Ortberg is an American business executive with an engineering background who became Boeing’s president and CEO in 2024. He previously led Rockwell Collins and the subsequently combined Collins Aerospace business, with experience in commercial and government aviation systems. At Boeing, his priorities include production stability, safety and quality, and corporate recovery.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026. Appointment decisions and effective dates, roles at different companies, and management goals and achieved results are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Rockwell Collins and took on leadership at Boeing, participating in aerospace manufacturing and corporate restructuring.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Iowa in 1982.
strings.facts.f2.label: Distinct roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Former chairman of Rockwell Collins; currently Boeing’s president, CEO and a director. Board membership is not described as chairmanship.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Aviation systems management
strings.highlights.h1.text: Advanced from program management into commercial and government systems leadership, then became CEO of an aerospace supplier.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Rebuilding safety and production systems
strings.highlights.h2.text: Testified before Congress and discussed Boeing’s safety and quality reforms; commitments and improvement plans do not establish that all regulatory issues have been resolved.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussed production stability and financial plans
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed 737 production stability in an interview following third-quarter results; future cash flow targets remain forecasts.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Testified before the Senate
strings.timeline.t2.text: Appeared before the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee to discuss company reforms, safety and quality, and restoring trust.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became Boeing president and CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Board’s July 30 appointment took effect that day; he also joined the Board.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led Collins Aerospace
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became CEO of the business after the integration of Rockwell Collins with United Technologies, serving until February 2020.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Rockwell Collins CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Having become president in 2012, assumed the additional duties of chief executive officer in 2013.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Rockwell Collins
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined as a program manager and subsequently took on broader management responsibilities.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Began his career at Texas Instruments
strings.timeline.t7.text: Entered the technology industry as an engineer.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earned a mechanical engineering degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from the University of Iowa, laying a professional foundation for later engineering and aerospace manufacturing management.
